Additionally, on the same date, Grupo Aval completed its acquisition of 40.77% of the ordinary shares of Casa de Bolsa S.A. from Corficolombiana S.A. and Organización Pajonales S.A.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (downgrade event and outlooks) and P3 (fiscal deficit figure and GDP growth).
risks.claim: Colombia's sovereign credit rating was downgraded to 'BB-' by S&P on April 8, 2026, amid a fiscal deficit of 6.4% of GDP, creating macroeconomic headwinds for the domestic banking sector.
quotes: On April 8, 2026, S&P Global Ratings downgraded Colombia's long-term foreign currency sovereign credit rating to 'BB-' from 'BB', and its long-term local currency rating to 'BB' from 'BB+'. The outlooks on both ratings are stable.
the deficit for 2025 closed at 6.4% of GDP and remains the main challenge of the country's economy.

risks.basis: Stated in P3 (rate path, expectations, NIM figures) and P2 (deposit structure and loan mix details).
risks.claim: The Central Bank halted its easing cycle at 9.25% and year-end 2026 rate expectations shifted to 11.75%, threatening the NIM recovery that underpinned 2025's 69.6% profit growth.
quotes: the year-end 2026 Central Bank rate expectations began to increase in tandem, shifting 5.25 percentage points to 11.75% in 12 months
After the government set a 23.7% minimum wage increase (including transportation subsidy) on December 29, 2025, inflation expectations have continued to price-in inflationary pressures.

risks.basis: Stated in P3 (MD&A discussion of asset quality metrics).
risks.claim: While overall net cost of risk fell 38 basis points in 2025, commercial loans slightly deteriorated, and loans past due over 90 days stood at 3.3%.
quotes: Net cost of risk decreased 38 basis points in 2025 mainly driven by an improvement in the asset quality of consumer portfolio, while commercial loans slightly deteriorated.
Loans past due more than 90 days were 3.3% at December 31, 2025, 77 basis points lower compared to December 31, 2024.

risks.basis: Stated in P3 (FX exposure figures) and P1 (MFG sale completion).
risks.claim: Grupo Aval holds U.S.$ 3.4 billion of long-term debt denominated in U.S. dollars, with 8.7% of loans and 7.8% of deposits in foreign currency, exposing it to COP depreciation risk.
quotes: At December 31, 2025, 8.7% of our loans and 7.8% of our deposits were denominated in foreign currency. On a consolidated basis, we had U.S.$ 3.4 billion (Ps 12.9 trillion) of long-term debt denominated in U.S. dollars as of December 31, 2025.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (risk factor section describing geopolitical events and their potential impact).
risks.claim: U.S. military strikes on Venezuela in January 2026 and renewed U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran in February 2026 create regional and global economic uncertainty that could affect Colombia's economy and Grupo Aval's operating environment.
quotes: On January 3, 2026, the United States launched a series of strikes against Venezuela and captured and removed former President Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, from the country.

After December 31, 2025, the United States and Israel carried out new strikes in February 2026 against Iran's nuclear and missile programs. Iran responded with attacks on Israel, U.S. bases in the region, and energy and civilian infrastructure in several Gulf states, causing sharp oil price volatility and supply chain disruptions.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (risk factor section on tax regulations).
risks.claim: Financial institutions in Colombia face a 40% corporate income tax rate from 2023 to 2027, five points above the general 35% rate, compressing after-tax returns.
quotes: In the case of financial institutions, such as Grupo Aval and our banking subsidiaries, such rate will be temporarily higher (40%), from 2023 to 2027.

risks.basis: Stated in P1 (Item 4, company history and milestones).
risks.claim: Banco de Bogotá's announced acquisition of Itaú's retail banking operations in Colombia and Panama, adding 277,000 clients with Ps. $6.5 trillion in loans, remains pending regulatory approval.
quotes: On December 23, 2025, Banco de Bogotá announced the acquisition of Itaú's retail banking operations in Colombia and Panama, adding 277,000 clients with Ps. $6.5 trillion in loans and Ps. $4.1 trillion in deposits, reinforcing its affluent segment focus and competitive positioning, pending regulatory approval.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (risk factor on liquidity) and P3 (fiscal deficit and TES yield data). F3 provides the operating cash flow counter.
risks.claim: Grupo Aval is exposed to liquidity risk associated with government funding impacted by a weak fiscal government position, with Colombia's 2025 fiscal deficit at 6.4% of GDP and 30-year TES yields increasing by 63 basis points between December 2024 and February 2026.
quotes: we are exposed to liquidity risk associated with government funding impacted by a weak fiscal government position

Impact from the persistently high fiscal account deficit led to an increase in yield of government debt (TES), as seen on the graph below, with 30-year yields increasing by 63 basis points between December 2024 and February 2026.
